title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Relevant Matters concerning the People's Courts' Setting Aside of Foreign-related Arbitral Awards
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Relevant Matters Concerning the People's Courts' Revocation of Foreign-Related Arbitral Awards

Fa [1998] No. 40

All High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

In order to strictly implement the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Arbitration Law) and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), and to ensure that litigation and arbitration activities are conducted in accordance with the law, it is hereby decided to establish a reporting system for the People's Courts' revocation of foreign-related arbitral awards of China. To this end, the following notice is given:

1. Where a party applies to a People's Court for revocation of a foreign-related arbitral award of China in accordance with the provisions of the Arbitration Law, if the People's Court, upon examination, considers that the foreign-related arbitral award falls under any of the circumstances set forth in Article 260, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, it must, before ruling to revoke the award or notifying the arbitral tribunal to re-arbitrate, submit the matter to the High People's Court in its jurisdiction for review. If the High People's Court agrees to revoke the award or to notify the arbitral tribunal to re-arbitrate, it shall submit its review opinion to the Supreme People's Court. Only after receiving a reply from the Supreme People's Court may the People's Court rule to revoke the award or notify the arbitral tribunal to re-arbitrate.

2. Where the People's Court accepting the application for revocation of the award considers that the award should be revoked or that the arbitral tribunal should be notified to re-arbitrate, it shall, within thirty days from the date of acceptance of the application, report to the High People's Court of its jurisdiction. If that High People's Court agrees to revoke the award or to notify the arbitral tribunal to re-arbitrate, it shall, within fifteen days, report to the Supreme People's Court so as to strictly comply with the provisions of Article 60 of the Arbitration Law.

April 23, 1998
